description: Foundation 1.0 — the vocabulary every backend LEGO declares itself in. This file is DATA, not a framework: it fixes the legal values for communication modes, operation semantics, runtimes, trust, resources, portability, lifecycle and node-creation routes, so a domain card is machine-checkable and an AI agent can retrieve one small card instead of reading the repository. Nothing here executes; tools/lego/* enforce it and apps/n8n-lego/src/lego/foundation.mjs reads it.

principles.contractAboveImplementation: The stable contract exists ABOVE JS/Rust/WASM. Rust is an implementation choice, never a new architecture, protocol, contract system or reason to split services. Choosing Rust must never require a compiler on a user device or break JS/community-node compatibility.
principles.cheapArchitecture: The architecture itself must stay cheap: direct call -> explicit contract -> lazy runtime -> worker only when necessary. No HTTP between local LEGO, no message bus for appearance, no always-on daemons, no duplicated registries.
principles.smallestViable: Prefer the smallest implementation that satisfies the contract. Declarative and community-compatible routes win when they are cheaper overall.
principles.lowEndFirst: Core must remain usable on a laptop, a small VPS, Termux and Android: small RAM, few cores, local storage. Heavy capability must be remote-capable rather than mandatory.

legoModel.tierRule: Domain LEGO -> Feature LEGO -> meaningful Sub-LEGO. Depth stays capped at 3 unless the Manager explicitly approves an exception. Not every function or helper becomes a LEGO: a LEGO earns its identity by owning a contract, data or state.
legoModel.granularityTest: If it has no independent contract, no independent owner and no independent lifecycle, it is a function — not a LEGO.

call.summary: Synchronous direct contract call. The DEFAULT for in-process communication.
call.transport: direct in-process function call, typed objects, no serialization
call.use: everything, unless another mode is specifically justified

event.summary: Asynchronous notification that something occurred or state changed.
event.transport: in-process emitter today; a worker boundary may serialize it later
event.use: state changes other LEGOs may care about; never for request/response

stream.summary: Continuous, ordered flow of items with backpressure.
stream.transport: async iterator in-process; a framed channel across a worker boundary
stream.use: execution output, logs, chat/AI token streams, large result sets

batch.summary: Many logical operations carried in one call to amortise overhead.
batch.transport: same as call; the unit is an array of operations
batch.use: high-frequency small operations, especially across a future worker boundary

rules: CALL is the default. A LEGO must not use EVENT or STREAM to avoid declaring a dependency.
No HTTP between local LEGO. HTTP appears only at a real process or trust boundary.
No message bus introduced to make the architecture look scalable.
A contract declares WHICH modes an operation supports; the transport is chosen by the host, not baked into the contract.
STREAM operations must declare a backpressure policy.
EVENT delivery is at-most-once in-process today; a consumer that needs durability must say so and is a P11 concern.
communication.defaultRule: CALL is the default. Any other mode must be justified by the semantics of the operation, never by a wish to look distributed.

transport.neutralityRule: A contract describes WHAT happens, not HOW it is transported. `execute(request)` must never become inherently `HTTP POST /execute`.
transport.bindingRule: Each target is a BINDING of the same logical contract. Adding a binding must never change the contract's operations, error codes or semantics.
transport.serializationRule: Direct in-process calls pass typed/structured objects with zero serialization. Only worker and remote bindings serialize, and only at the boundary.

envelope.summary: A lightweight logical envelope carried alongside a request. Optional by design: a direct call may pass nothing, and an absent envelope must never change semantics.

fields.contractVersion: version the caller was built against
fields.correlationId: groups related requests (one user action, one execution)
fields.causationId: identifies the immediate parent request that caused this one (a derived envelope defaults it to the parent requestId)
fields.traceId: distributed trace identity, for a future worker topology
fields.actor: security context: who is asking, with which scopes
fields.deadline: absolute epoch-ms after which the callee should stop
fields.idempotencyKey: de-duplication key for retryable, non-idempotent operations

envelope.costRule: The envelope must impose no serialization cost on direct calls. It is a plain object passed by reference in-process, and only serialized at a worker/remote boundary — where `signal` is dropped and replaced by a cancellation message.

idempotency.rule: Any operation a worker or retry policy may re-issue must declare one of these. `idempotent-with-key` requires the envelope's idempotencyKey.

determinism.rule: Determinism class decides whether an operation can be replayed and compared. It is the precondition for comparing a JS implementation against a future Rust one.

atomicity.rule: Local transaction boundaries and compensation only. No distributed transactions.

concurrency.rule: Metadata only. No global scheduler is created; the host may honour it when one exists.

backpressure.rule: Declared per STREAM operation so no LEGO invents its own backpressure logic.

cancellation.rule: Every potentially blocking operation must accept a deadline and a cancellation signal. No LEGO may wait indefinitely without a declared policy.

verified.summary: Reviewed/signed third party. In-process where its capabilities allow.

community.summary: Unreviewed community code. Restricted compatibility environment.

untrusted.summary: Unknown or hostile. Sandbox or worker only.

trust.rule: Trust level and capabilities are SEPARATE. A high trust level never implicitly grants a capability; every capability is granted explicitly and is checked at the boundary.

js-compat.summary: Compatibility runtime for existing n8n/community JavaScript nodes.
js-compat.note: Community nodes MUST keep loading. This runtime is why a node never has to be rewritten to keep working.

rust-native.summary: Native Rust implementation behind the same contract.
rust-native.note: Ships as a PREBUILT artifact. A Rust compiler must never be required on a user device.

wasm.summary: WASM module, portable and sandboxed by construction.
wasm.note: Preferred where portability or isolation matters more than peak speed.

remote-worker.summary: Execution mode rather than a runtime: the same contract executed elsewhere.
remote-worker.note: The escape hatch that lets a constrained device still offer a heavy node.

runtimes.selectionRule: Runtime selection belongs to Node Runtime Resolution and is never mandatory for every node. A node declares what it NEEDS; the host decides what it GETS.

portability.rule: A node may exist on a constrained device even when it must execute remotely — `remote-capable` is what makes Android/Termux viable without shrinking the catalog.

resources.rule: Metadata and policy input, not a scheduler. It exists so the AI route decision and a future activation policy have real numbers instead of guesses.

activation.rule: Installed != loaded != active. Nothing is forced into RAM. This is the property that keeps the runtime usable on a low-end laptop, a small VPS, Termux and Android.

failureBoundaries.rule: A failure inside a dangerous or untrusted LEGO must never be able to take down trusted core infrastructure. Trust level and failure boundary are chosen together.
failureBoundaries.fallbackRule: Fallback to another implementation is permitted ONLY when both implementations satisfy the same contract version — semantic compatibility is a contract statement, not a hope.

classes.persistent: survives restart; belongs to a data owner; must go through a storage contract
classes.runtime: lives for the process/session; must be explicitly declared
classes.cache: derivable and discardable; must declare TTL, scope and invalidation
classes.configuration: injected at the edge, never read from the environment inside a domain
classes.derived: computed from other state; never a source of truth

rules: Every meaningful domain declares a dataOwner and a stateOwner.
No hidden global mutable state. Process-local state is legal only when classified as cache or runtime-transient.
Storage is an infrastructure contract — never a licence for one LEGO to reach into another LEGO's persistence internals.
A cache is owned. There is no universal global cache.

replay.rule: Lightweight by design: capture the declared inputs and the determinism class, replay against another implementation, compare outputs. This is the mechanism that will validate a Rust implementation against the JS one. No time-travel infrastructure is built now.
replay.comparableWhen: determinism is `deterministic`, or `external-state-dependent` with its external reads captured

checkpoint.rule: Checkpointing is opt-in. Defaulting to `always` would grow disk without consent, which breaks the low-end promise.

caching.rule: A cache declares its owner and invalidation. `shared` scope requires a storage contract, because a process-local cache is invisible to a second worker.

observability.rule: Instrument LEGO BOUNDARIES only. Instrumenting every internal function is both a performance cost and a coupling risk.

audit.rule: Audit records architectural change only. It is deliberately low-volume and is not application logging.

rollout.rule: A future-neutral model for running an old and a new implementation side by side behind one contract. No feature-flag platform is installed; the stages are vocabulary the replacement lifecycle already supports.
rollout.precondition: Both implementations satisfy the same contract version — otherwise it is a migration, not a rollout.

low-end-vps.note: the floor the core must fit inside

deviceProfile.rule: Used later by the AI route decision and by Execution to choose local vs WASM vs Rust vs remote. It is input to a policy, not a scheduler.

glossary.LEGO: A unit of architecture with one owner, one reason to change, a public contract and a private implementation. Not every function is a LEGO.
glossary.Domain LEGO: A top-level LEGO representing a bounded area of the system.
glossary.Feature LEGO: A LEGO nested inside a domain, composed by its parent.
glossary.Sub-LEGO: A LEGO nested inside a feature. Depth 3 is the cap unless the Manager approves an exception.
glossary.Public contract: The only surface another LEGO may use. Stable, versioned, locked.
glossary.Private implementation: Everything else. Replaceable at any time without a contract version change.
glossary.Contract version: A promise. Major = breaking, minor = additive, patch = behaviour-preserving.
glossary.Contract lock: The file recording each public contract's current version, so drift is mechanically detectable.
glossary.Envelope: The metadata carried alongside every operation: identity, correlation, deadline, cancellation, idempotency, actor. Zero cost on direct in-process calls.
glossary.Transport neutrality: The same logical contract works in-process, in a worker, over WASM or remotely. `execute(request)` must never become inherently `HTTP POST /execute`.
glossary.Capability: A declared ability. Feature capabilities describe what a LEGO offers; security capabilities (network, filesystem, subprocess, secrets, native, env) must be granted explicitly.
glossary.Trust level: How much the system believes in the code: core, verified, community, untrusted. Trust never implies a capability.
glossary.Failure boundary: How far a failure can travel: in-process-safe, sandboxed, worker-isolated. Untrusted code must never be able to kill the trusted core.
glossary.Data owner: The single LEGO that owns a dataset. Others read it through its contract, never through its persistence.
glossary.State class: persistent, runtime, cache, configuration or derived. Unclassified hidden global state is forbidden.
glossary.Blast radius: How many other LEGOs a change can reach. Drives test selection.
glossary.Strangler boundary: The controlled edge around the legacy aggregate. It may shrink, never grow.
glossary.Quarantine: The mandatory holding state for a failed or suspect node. Evidence before deletion.
glossary.Replay: Capture inputs, replay them against another implementation, compare outputs. The mechanism that would make a JS-to-Rust swap provable.
glossary.Activation: available -> loaded -> active -> idle -> unloaded -> disabled. Nothing is forced into RAM.

minimalCore.rule: The core is only these five. Everything else — nodes, chat, translation, AI providers, workers — is optional and loaded lazily. A feature that cannot be removed without breaking boot is a core member and must be justified as one.
minimalCore.test: If the system cannot boot without it, it is core. If it can, it must not be in core.

rules: The system must start and run useful workflows with no network available.
No step of installation or execution may require a compiler on an end-user device.
Binary artifacts (Rust, WASM) are PREBUILT and downloaded per platform, or the feature degrades to a portable implementation.
A node that cannot run locally declares `remote-capable` rather than disappearing from the catalog.
Nothing is loaded into memory until it is activated.
offlineReadiness.artifactRule: Portable build artifacts are a hard requirement for any native implementation. `isRustJustified()` refuses a migration without them.

chatContract.shape: Chat Contract ├ native chat provider └ Hermes provider
chatContract.rule: Hermes is a FUTURE OPTIONAL capability behind the Chat Contract. It must never become a core dependency, must never be required for boot, and no LEGO may import it directly — a consumer talks to the Chat Contract and neither knows nor cares which provider answers.
chatContract.why: Reserving the slot costs nothing and prevents the far more expensive mistake of wiring a specific provider into the core later.
chatContract.notBuilt: No chat provider, no Hermes integration and no translation LEGO exists. This is a named empty slot, deliberately.

deferred: unsafe-runtime-capability and unrestricted-resource-access need a runtime that does not exist yet
securityGate.rule: Enforcement stays lightweight: cheap textual and manifest checks at contract boundaries. This is a gate, not a static analyser, and it must never become slow enough that people skip it.
